subject: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.com>, Bob Chen <bob.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up

Hi Alice / Bob 

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps on the performance/SLO items we discussed so engineering can size the right capacity and rate limits: 

Summary of requirements we captured:
- Latency SLOs: p95 generation latency target = 250ms for non-streaming short responses (<=150 tokens); for streaming use-case, p95 first-byte <= 150ms and per-chunk <= 100ms.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state QPS = 600 requests/min (10 rps), peak bursts up to ~2,000 requests/min (33 rps) for marketing spikes.
- Concurrency: client-side we expect ~500 concurrent active connections during normal peak, up to 3,000 concurrent during large events.
- Streaming: yes  long-lived streaming connections for progressive responses (~150 tokens avg per response, chunked every 50 tokens).
- Connection pooling: clients will use connection reuse and keep-alive, but may open up to 50 parallel connections per application node.

Open questions / items we need from you to finalize a proposal:
1) Confirm the expected average tokens returned per request and the percent of calls that will use streaming vs full-response.
2) Share a 24h traffic shape (CSV or the SLO_requirements.xlsx I attached) showing baseline vs peak by minute if possible.
3) Let us know whether cross-region failover is required (we discussed U.S. only for now).

What Redwood can offer next:
- We can file an accelerated quota request for an elevated rate limit and concurrency seat while we validate traffic.
- For sustained peaks at the numbers above we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) to guarantee concurrency and lower unit cost; otherwise we can provision a temporary elevated quota for hosted with a short evaluation window.

Next steps:
- Alice/Bob: share the traffic CSV + confirm tokens/streaming split by EOD Fri (July 17).
- Marissa: I'll loop in engineering (Dev + Michael) to propose initial quota numbers and a follow-up SRE sync.

Attaching SLO_requirements.xlsx and a one-pager Redwood_SLA_Summary.pdf to this thread.

Thanks F
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0123
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Chen <bob.chen@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up

Thanks Marissa  good notes. A few clarifications from our side after I checked with the infra team: 

- Average tokens per response: ~140 tokens; 65% of calls will use streaming (progressive tokens), 35% request the full response at once.
- Expected steady-state: 1,500 requests/hour (~25 rps) across our EU + US users; we had quoted the lower number earlier because that was per-service. Total aggregate for this feature is closer to what you see here.
- Concurrency: our realistic goal for the first 90 days is 800 concurrent connections across users, but we need the system to handle event-driven spikes up to 3,000 concurrent for up to 10 minutes.
- Connection pooling: our app servers will keep connections alive and reuse them; however due to many small app nodes we may open ~30–50 parallel connections per node.

I've attached an export (SLO_requirements.xlsx) with a minute-level spike sample for the demo day on July 30. Let me know if you need anything else to size.

Best,
Alice
VP, Product | Acme Robotics

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up

Alice  thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications and proposal from Redwood: 

1) We interpret your numbers as aggregate QPS ~25 rps baseline with short spikes to ~55 rps during event windows; concurrent connection target 800 steady, 3,000 burst for ~10 minutes. That aligns with our previous notes.
2) For streaming-heavy workloads (65% streaming), the main capacity factor is connection concurrency + per-connection token throughput rather than pure QPS.

Proposal (next step):
- I'll open an elevated hosted quota request for a 90-day evaluation window to 4,000 concurrent connections and 100 rps sustained (burst to 200 rps) while we run a controlled load test. This gives room for your worst-case spikes while we confirm token throughput.
- If traffic is sustained at those levels beyond 90 days, we recommend Redwood Dedicated  we can provide a cost estimate once SRE validates the exact GPU footprint from your token/sequence profile.

Can Dev / Michael confirm feasibility on our side and whether we should route this to Dedicated right away? Also proposing a 30-minute SRE sync next Tue (Jul 20) to walk through load test scenarios.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: ACME concurrency + quota sizing (please review)

Team 

Please review Alice's traffic export and the summary above. Key asks:
- Confirm whether elevated hosted quota to 4,000 concurrent / 200 rps burst is safe to provision for a 90-day evaluation.
- If not, propose initial Dedicated sizing (GPU count estimate + expected slot concurrency) and a quick cost delta for the proposal she can take to procurement.
- Michael: can you run a back-of-envelope on token throughput for 65% streaming @ 140 tokens avg and advise if connection-level limits (per-connection tokens/s) will be the gating factor?

I attached the SLO_requirements.xlsx; I can pull in legal/procurement once we have a recommendation.

Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME concurrency + quota sizing (please review)

Thanks Marissa  quick read and proposed plan: 

- Elevated hosted quota: I think we can safely approve a temporary hosted quota for 4,000 concurrent connections for a 90-day evaluation, provided we gate it behind an operational playbook (rate-limited ramp, synthetic load test, and an SRE runbook if we observe error rates >1%).
- Token throughput: with 65% streaming at ~140 tokens avg, expected token/sec per connection during an active response is modest (roughly 5 tokens/s depending on model and chunking). The bigger factor will be simultaneous active responses. For the numbers provided (peak 3,000 concurrent), we should assume worst-case active response concurrency ~2,000 connections.
- Dedicated recommendation: for sustained traffic beyond the evaluation, start sizing for 24 GPUs (A100x or equivalent) depending on chosen model; that typically maps to ~1,500,000 effective concurrent response capacity with batching/kv cache benefits. I'll finalize exact GPU counts after Dev runs a short perf test with the attached spike CSV.

I'll draft the SRE ramp plan and upload a one-pager to the drive link. For now we can tell Acme we can proceed with a 90-day elevated hosted quota + SRE sync next Tue (Jul 20 10:00am PT).

-Michael
